name: slack-mcp
label: Slack (MCP)
description: Slack through Slack's MCP server, read only: messages that mention you, and `door slack …` for Copilot chats. You log in from Settings; no token to paste.

SLACK_MCP_CLIENT_ID.label: Slack app client ID
SLACK_MCP_CLIENT_ID.hint: From the Slack app your workspace uses for MCP (Basic Information → App Credentials).Slack's MCP server only takes registered apps, so ask your Slack admins for the client ID if you don't have an app of your own. The app needs the redirect URL below under OAuth & Permissions, and PKCE turned on (or set the client secret).
SLACK_MCP_CLIENT_ID.patternHint: a Slack client ID looks like 1234567890.1234567890

SLACK_MCP_CLIENT_SECRET.label: Client secret (optional)
SLACK_MCP_CLIENT_SECRET.hint: Only for an app without PKCE.

SLACK_MCP_REDIRECT_URI.label: Redirect URL
SLACK_MCP_REDIRECT_URI.hint: Must match the app's. http://localhost:19876/callback if empty.

SLACK_MCP_SCOPES.label: Scopes
SLACK_MCP_SCOPES.hint: Read-only scopes if empty.Space-separated user scopes asked for at login. The default reads channels, DMs, group DMs, search, files, canvases, lists, reactions, emoji and users; it has no chat:write, and the door refuses tools that write either way.

SLACK_MCP_QUERY.label: Mentions search
SLACK_MCP_QUERY.hint: Slack search for the rows under Needs you. <@{me}> after:{after} if empty.{me} is your Slack user and {after} the day the window starts (CLEARSKY_MENTION_DAYS). Add to it with Slack's search syntax, or point it at something else entirely.

secrets.note: your Slack user token from the browser login (and its refresh token), in ~/.config/clearsky/slack-mcp-token.json, readable by you only

doors.name: slack
doors.about: reads Slack as you through Slack's MCP server (search, channels, threads, people, canvases, files); tools that send or change anything are refused

note: Reads only. The login opens Slack in your browser and comes back to a callback on localhost; every chat call is in Copilot's changes.
outside: It logs in in your browser with a callback on localhost and holds the Slack login for chats, which is what a door is for.
